content:
alex: Quick heads-up — PR #11800 is showing a failing CI on linux-ubuntu-22.04: snapshot mismatch in tests/encoder/beam_encoder.test.js. Not obvious if it's flaky or a small regression.

ci-bot: buildkite/build-1283 — failed — step: test:unit — job: linux-ubuntu-22.04 — failing tests: tests/encoder/beam_encoder.test.js (snapshot) — logs: https://ci.redwood/example/1283

cj: I can take a look in ~20m. If it's just a snapshot diff maybe we need to update with `yarn test -u` after confirming output correctness.

alex: Thanks. I ran the failing test locally in Docker and got the same diff. Paste of the relevant snippet: 
```
- expected: 
+ received: 
- "<beam start>tokenized|A|B|C"
+ "<beam start>tokenized|A|B|C|"
```
Seems like an extra trailing pipe character showed up.

beatrice: That trailing pipe rings a bell — we changed the tokenizer pad behavior in the latest model patch. Could be a legit change. Which commit pins the model weights in this PR?

alex: PR touches inference/encoder.js but the model pinned in package.json still points to `model@v2.3.1`. The tokenizer change was in the model release v2.3.2, so mismatch possible.

samira: If the code expects v2.3.1 behavior, updating snapshots is wrong. We should either pin the code to accept new tokenizer output (preferred) or pin the model to v2.3.1 for the PR. What risk level is this change?

alex: The change is small — strip trailing separators from encoder output. I think accepting new tokenizer output and updating snapshots is ok, but want a second pair of eyes. Will add a tiny normalization in encoder.js to be defensive.

ci-bot: buildkite/build-1284 — triggered by @cj — queued rerun for linux-ubuntu-22.04 tests.

cj: Kicked off a rerun. If green, will request snapshot review from @beatrice and then @dave for approval to merge.

beatrice: I can review snapshots once the rerun finishes. If it's just consistent new trailing pipe, prefer code fix over snapshot update. If alex adds normalization, that should keep snapshots stable.

dave: Pinged. I'm around for approvals this afternoon PST. If the rerun is green and there's a clear fix, I can +1 and merge.

alex: Will push the defensive change in a minute (`encoder: stripTrailingSeparators`) and add a unit that would have caught this. Then I'll force-push to the branch.

cj: Cool. After push I'll re-run CI again (automated). If it still flakes, we'll open a short-term revert or pin PR.

ci-bot: buildkite/build-1285 — started — running tests on linux-ubuntu-22.04.

alex: pushed fix and test. Command I ran locally: `docker run --rm -v $PWD:/app node:18 bash -c "yarn && yarn test tests/encoder/beam_encoder.test.js"` — passed locally.

samira: Thanks for the detail. Also adding a note in the PR description about model/version assumptions would help avoid confusion later.

cj: Rerun is green on linux, windows also passed. Only mac had unrelated snapshot noise. I'll merge when @dave gives final approval and CI stays green for 10m.

beatrice: Reviewed diff, defensive normalization looks good. No behavioral regressions observed in sample prompts I tried.

dave: +1 — merging now. Reminder: will watch canary deploy for 30m after merge.

ci-bot: buildkite/build-1286 — merge event processed. Canary deploy queued.

alex: Thanks everyone. Leaving a follow-up comment in the PR about the model version note and a test that asserts stable tokenization output to avoid future flakes. :thumbsup:

cj: Nice. Filing a small tasks ticket to add a CI healthcheck that runs the encoder snapshot against the pinned model nightly to catch drifting model/tokenizer combos. @samira assigning to infra backlog.

samira: Got it — creating ticket INFRA-402.

alex: Thread resolved for me. If anything else shows up I'll reopen.
